easy.def: A word used to show two things at the same time.
examples: I sang as I walked.
She smiled as she hugged him.
The sun set as we ate.

more.def: A word used to show that two things happen at the same time, or that one thing is the reason for another.
examples: The audience clapped as the dancers took a bow.
As it was raining, we had the party indoors.
He hummed a tune as he washed the dishes.

easy.def: A word used to show what someone or something is or does.
examples: She works as a nurse.
I used a box as a chair.
He dressed as a pirate.

more.def: A word used to show the job, role, or purpose of someone or something.
examples: My aunt works as a firefighter in our town.
We used a blanket as a tent in the living room.
The famous dog served as a mascot for the team.

easy.def: To go up.
examples: The balloon will ascend.
We ascend the stairs.
The bird ascended into the sky.

more.def: To rise or climb up.
examples: The hot air balloon slowly ascended into the clouds.
The climbers ascended the steep mountain trail.
Smoke ascended from the campfire into the night air.

easy.def: Going up.
examples: The ascending path is steep.
The ascending balloon.
Put the numbers in ascending order.

more.def: Going up, or arranged from the lowest to the highest.
examples: The ascending path wound up the mountain.
Put the numbers in ascending order, from least to greatest.
The ascending balloon grew smaller.

easy.def: A climb up.
examples: The ascent was hard.
We began the ascent.
The ascent took hours.

more.def: The act of going up, such as climbing a mountain.
examples: The ascent of the mountain took two days.
We made a slow ascent up the steep path.
The rocket's ascent was swift.

easy.def: To find out for sure.
examples: We ascertained the time.
She ascertained the facts.
He ascertained the answer.

more.def: To find out something for certain.
examples: We called to ascertain what time the shop opens.
The detective ascertained the facts.
Scientists ascertain the age of fossils.

easy.def: Feeling bad because you did something wrong.
examples: I felt ashamed of my lie.
He was ashamed of what he said.
She looked ashamed.

more.def: Feeling sorry and a little embarrassed about something you did.
examples: He was ashamed that he had broken the window.
She felt ashamed of how she shouted at her friend.
Do not be ashamed to ask for help when you need it.

easy.def: Gray, like ashes.
examples: His face was ashen.
The sky was ashen.
She looked ashen.

more.def: Very pale, like ashes, often from fear or shock.
examples: His face turned ashen when he saw the spider.
The ashen sky promised snow.
She looked ashen after the news.

easy.def: The gray powder that is left after something burns.
examples: The fire left ashes.
We cleaned out the ashes.
The ashes are gray.

more.def: The soft gray powder that remains after something has burned.
examples: The campfire left a pile of ashes.
We swept the ashes out of the fireplace.
The ashes were still warm.

easy.def: On or to the land from the sea.
examples: The boat came ashore.
We swam ashore.
The sailors went ashore.

more.def: To or onto the land from the water.
examples: The boat came ashore at dawn.
Waves carried the driftwood ashore.
The sailors went ashore for supplies.

easy.def: Gray, like ashes from a fire.
examples: The sky was ashy.
His face looked ashy.
Ashy gray.

more.def: Covered with ashes, or pale gray like ashes.
examples: The sky turned an ashy gray.
His face looked ashy from fright.
The ashy fireplace needed a sweep.

easy.def: To one side.
examples: Please move aside.
I put the book aside.
She stepped aside.

more.def: To one side, or out of the way.
examples: He stepped aside to let the others pass.
Set your work aside and come to dinner.
She put some money aside for a new bike.

easy.def: To say something so someone will answer.
examples: I ask my teacher.
She asked a question.
Ask Dad for help.

more.def: To put a question to someone, or to request something from someone.
examples: I asked the librarian where the animal books are.
He asked his grandmother to tell the story again.
May I ask you a question about the experiment?

easy.def: With doubt.
examples: She looked askance.
He glanced askance.
They looked askance at him.

more.def: With doubt or suspicion, often with a sideways glance.
examples: She looked askance at the strange food.
He glanced askance at the stranger.
They looked askance at the odd plan.

easy.def: Not straight.
examples: The picture hung askew.
His hat was askew.
The sign was askew.

more.def: Not straight; tilted to one side.
examples: The picture hung askew on the wall.
His hat sat askew on his head.
The wind left the sign askew.

easy.def: Sleeping.
examples: The baby is asleep.
The cat is asleep.
I fell asleep in the car.

more.def: In a state of sleep; not awake.
examples: The baby fell asleep in the car.
The whole house was asleep by midnight.
My legs fell asleep after I sat for a long time.

easy.def: A green vegetable that grows in long, thin stalks.
examples: We ate asparagus.
The asparagus is green.
Mom cooked asparagus.

more.def: A vegetable with long, thin green stalks and a tip like a bud.
examples: We steamed asparagus for dinner.
The asparagus stalks poked out of the garden.
Asparagus is cut when it is tender.

easy.def: One part of something.
examples: That is one aspect of the problem.
The aspect is new.
Each aspect is important.

more.def: One part or feature of something.
examples: One aspect of the story I liked was the setting.
The best aspect of the trip was the beach.
Look at every aspect of the plan.

easy.def: A tree with leaves that shake in the wind.
examples: The aspen shook.
Aspens are tall.
I saw an aspen.

more.def: A tall tree with smooth pale bark and round leaves that tremble in the slightest wind.
examples: The leaves of the aspen turned gold in the fall.
An aspen grove shimmered in the breeze.
Aspens grow in cool mountain forests.

easy.def: The black, hard stuff used to make roads.
examples: The road is asphalt.
I rode on the asphalt.
The asphalt is hot.

more.def: A black, sticky material mixed with stones that is used to cover roads.
examples: The workers covered the road with fresh asphalt.
The asphalt was hot under the summer sun.
We drew with chalk on the asphalt.

easy.def: A big hope or goal.
examples: Her aspiration is to fly.
He has an aspiration.
It is my aspiration.

more.def: A strong hope or ambition to achieve something.
examples: Her aspiration is to become an astronaut.
He has high aspirations.
My aspiration is to write a book.

easy.def: To hope to do something great.
examples: I aspire to be a doctor.
She aspires to sing.
He aspired to fly.

more.def: To have a strong wish to do or be something great.
examples: I aspire to be an astronaut.
She aspires to play the violin.
He aspired to be a champion.

easy.def: Hoping to become something.
examples: An aspiring artist.
The aspiring singer practiced.
He is an aspiring chef.

more.def: Hoping and working to become a certain kind of person.
examples: The aspiring singer practiced every day.
An aspiring artist painted on the sidewalk.
She is an aspiring chef who bakes every weekend.

easy.def: To put together.
examples: I assemble the toy.
They assembled the bike.
We assemble the model.

more.def: To put the parts of something together, or to gather people together.
examples: Dad assembled the bike from the box.
We assembled the model airplane.
The students assembled in the gym.

easy.def: A meeting of a lot of people.
examples: We went to an assembly.
The school assembly is in the gym.
The assembly was long.

more.def: A gathering of many people for a purpose, such as at a school.
examples: We went to a school assembly in the gym.
The principal spoke at the assembly.
The assembly sang a song.

easy.def: Putting parts together.
examples: The assembly of the toy took an hour.
Assembly is easy.
The assembly line.

more.def: The act of putting the parts of something together.
examples: The assembly of the bike took an hour.
The factory has an assembly line.
The kit came with assembly instructions.

easy.def: To agree.
examples: She assented to the plan.
He assented with a nod.
They assented.

more.def: To say yes or agree to something.
examples: She assented to the plan with a nod.
The class assented to the new rule.
He assented to going home early.

easy.def: To say something strongly.
examples: She will assert that she is right.
He asserted he was first.
I assert it is mine.

more.def: To state something firmly and confidently.
examples: She asserted that her answer was correct.
The boy asserted that he had not eaten the cookie.
The scientist asserted that the plant needed more light.

easy.def: Speaking up with confidence.
examples: She is assertive.
An assertive child spoke.
He was assertive.

more.def: Speaking up for yourself in a confident way.
examples: She was assertive and asked for what she needed.
An assertive child asked a question.
He was assertive but polite.

easy.def: To think about how good or how big something is.
examples: The teacher will assess my work.
They assessed the damage.
We assess the plan.

more.def: To carefully judge or decide the size, quality or importance of something.
examples: The teacher assessed our stories and gave each one a grade.
After the storm, workers assessed the damage to the roof.
The doctor assessed how well my arm was healing.

easy.def: A test or a careful look at how well something is doing.
examples: We took an assessment.
The teacher made an assessment.
The assessment was easy.

more.def: A careful judgment of how good, big or important something is, or a test that checks what you have learned.
examples: Our teacher gave us a reading assessment to see how well we read.
The workers made an assessment of the damage to the roof.
The doctor's assessment was that I was healthy.

easy.def: Something useful or valuable.
examples: Her smile is an asset.
The team's best asset.
A good asset.

more.def: Something that is useful or valuable to a person or group.
examples: Her kind smile is her best asset.
Speed is a great asset for a runner.
The school's library is a valuable asset.

easy.def: To give someone a job to do.
examples: The teacher assigned a project.
She assigned me a chore.
Mom assigns the jobs.

more.def: To give someone a job or task to do.
examples: The teacher assigned a book to read.
She assigned each child a job.
Mom assigned me to feed the dog.

easy.def: Work that a teacher tells you to do.
examples: Our assignment is to read a book.
The assignment is due tomorrow.
I finished my assignment.

more.def: A piece of work that someone gives you to do.
examples: Our assignment is to write a story about a pet.
The science assignment is due on Friday.
I finished the assignment before dinner.

easy.def: To help.
examples: I assist my teacher.
She assisted the nurse.
He assisted with the cooking.

more.def: To help someone do something.
examples: I assisted the teacher by handing out papers.
The nurse assisted the doctor.
He assisted the old woman across the street.

easy.def: Help.
examples: I need assistance.
She asked for assistance.
The nurse gave assistance.

more.def: Help or support that someone gives you.
examples: I need assistance with my homework.
The firefighters came to give assistance.
He asked for assistance with the heavy box.

easy.def: A person who helps.
examples: The teacher has an assistant.
I am his assistant.
The assistant carried the box.

more.def: A person who helps someone do a job.
examples: The teacher's assistant passed out papers.
The chef's assistant chopped the carrots.
The doctor's assistant took my temperature.

easy.def: To connect things in your mind.
examples: I associate summer with swimming.
She associates that song with her grandmother.
We associate red with stop.

more.def: To connect one thing to another in your mind.
examples: I associate the smell of bread with my grandma.
Many people associate the color red with danger.
She associates the song with her grandfather.

easy.def: A group of people with a shared purpose.
examples: I joined an association.
The association meets monthly.
The sports association planned a game.

more.def: An organization of people who have the same job or interest.
examples: My parents joined the neighborhood association.
The soccer association plans the games.
The nurses' association met on Friday.

easy.def: Of different kinds.
examples: We ate assorted candy.
Assorted fruit sat there.
The box of assorted crayons.

more.def: Of several different kinds mixed together.
examples: We ate assorted cookies from the tin.
The shop sold assorted hats.
A box of assorted pens sat on the desk.

easy.def: A mix of different kinds.
examples: An assortment of candy.
The box had an assortment.
I picked from the assortment.

more.def: A mixture of different kinds of things.
examples: The box held an assortment of candies.
The shop has an assortment of hats.
She picked from the assortment of colors.

easy.def: To think something is true without checking.
examples: I assume you are hungry.
She assumed it was Monday.
We assume it will rain.

more.def: To think that something is true without knowing for sure.
examples: I assumed the store was open, but it was closed.
Do not assume everyone likes spicy food.
She assumed the bus was late.

easy.def: Something you think is true without checking.
examples: It was just my assumption.
We made the wrong assumption.
Her assumption was right.

more.def: Something you accept as true without having proof that it is.
examples: I made the assumption that the store was open, but it was closed.
A scientist tests every assumption before calling it a fact.
It was a wrong assumption to think the test would be easy.

easy.def: A promise that makes you feel sure.
examples: He gave me his assurance.
Her assurance helped.
I have your assurance.

more.def: A promise or statement that tells someone not to worry.
examples: He gave me his assurance that the bridge was safe.
The nurse's assurance made the boy feel better.
She spoke with assurance and confidence.

easy.def: To tell someone it will be all right.
examples: I assure you it is safe.
She assured me.
He assured the child.

more.def: To tell someone that something is true so they will not worry.
examples: I assure you the dog is friendly.
She assured me she would be on time.
The nurse assured him it would not hurt.

easy.def: For sure.
examples: It will assuredly rain.
He assuredly will come.
She is assuredly right.

more.def: Certainly; without any doubt.
examples: It will assuredly rain tomorrow.
She will assuredly be there.
That is assuredly the best pie.

easy.def: A star-shaped garden flower.
examples: An aster bloomed.
The aster is purple.
Asters grow in fall.

more.def: A garden flower with many narrow petals around a yellow center that blooms in autumn.
examples: Purple asters bloomed along the fence in October.
Bees visit the aster for nectar.
The aster looks like a small star.

easy.def: At or toward the back of a ship.
examples: The wake was astern.
The captain looked astern.
Go astern.

more.def: At or toward the back of a ship or boat.
examples: The captain looked astern and saw the lighthouse fade.
A trail of foam stretched astern.
The lifeboat was towed astern.

easy.def: A big rock that moves in space.
examples: An asteroid flew by.
The asteroid is rocky.
Asteroids float in space.

more.def: A large rock that orbits the sun, found mostly between the planets Mars and Jupiter.
examples: An asteroid is a rocky object that travels around the sun.
Most asteroids are found in a belt between Mars and Jupiter.
Scientists track asteroids to see where they are heading.

easy.def: A health problem that makes it hard to breathe sometimes.
examples: My friend has asthma.
Asthma makes breathing hard.
She uses a puffer for asthma.

more.def: A condition of the lungs that can make it hard to breathe, causing coughing and wheezing.
examples: My friend has asthma and uses an inhaler.
Asthma can make it hard to breathe when you run fast.
Cold air can make asthma worse for some people.

easy.def: To surprise very much.
examples: The trick astonished me.
It astonishes him.
The size astonished us.

more.def: To surprise someone greatly.
examples: The magician's trick astonished the crowd.
Her speed astonished us.
It astonishes me how tall the tree has grown.

easy.def: Very surprised.
examples: I was astonished.
The astonished boy stared.
We were astonished by the trick.

more.def: Very surprised and amazed.
examples: I was astonished when I saw the huge cake.
The astonished audience gasped at the magic trick.
He was astonished to find a puppy on the porch.

easy.def: In a surprising way.
examples: He ran astonishingly fast.
The cake was astonishingly big.
She sang astonishingly well.

more.def: In a way that is very surprising.
examples: He ran astonishingly fast for a boy his age.
The tree was astonishingly tall.
She sang astonishingly well.

easy.def: Great surprise.
examples: She stared in astonishment.
His astonishment was clear.
The magic trick filled us with astonishment.

more.def: A feeling of great surprise.
examples: She stared at the huge cake in astonishment.
His face showed his astonishment.
The crowd gasped in astonishment.

easy.def: Very surprised.
examples: She was astounded.
He looked astounded.
We were astounded by the trick.

more.def: Extremely surprised.
examples: The children were astounded by the magician's trick.
She was astounded to see how tall the tree had grown.
We were astounded at the size of the whale.

easy.def: Away from the right path.
examples: The sheep went astray.
The ball went astray.
He led us astray.

more.def: Away from the right path or the right way.
examples: The sheep wandered astray from the flock.
The ball went astray and landed in the neighbor's yard.
The wrong map led us astray.

easy.def: With a leg on each side.
examples: He sat astride the log.
He rode astride.
They sat astride the fence.

more.def: With one leg on each side of something.
examples: She sat astride the horse.
He sat astride the fence.
The boy sat astride his bike.

easy.def: An old tool used to find the position of the stars.
examples: The sailor used an astrolabe.
An astrolabe is old.
The astrolabe shows stars.

more.def: An old instrument used to measure the position of the sun and stars, used by sailors long ago.
examples: The sailor used an astrolabe to find his way.
An astrolabe helps measure the height of the stars.
The museum had an old brass astrolabe.

easy.def: A belief that the stars can tell about your life.
examples: Astrology uses stars.
She reads astrology.
Astrology is not science.

more.def: The belief that the positions of the stars and planets affect people's lives.
examples: Some people read astrology in the newspaper.
Astrology is a belief, not a science.
He learned about astrology and the signs of the zodiac.

easy.def: A person who goes into space.
examples: The astronaut waved from the rocket.
I want to be an astronaut one day.
The astronaut floats in space.

more.def: A person trained to travel and work in space.
examples: The astronaut lived on the space station for six months.
An astronaut wears a special suit to stay safe outside the ship.
The astronauts fixed the telescope while circling the Earth.

easy.def: A scientist who studies stars and planets.
examples: The astronomer used a telescope.
An astronomer looks at stars.
My aunt is an astronomer.

more.def: A scientist who studies stars, planets and outer space.
examples: The astronomer looked at the moon through a telescope.
An astronomer discovered a new comet.
The astronomer explained how stars are born.

easy.def: About stars and planets, or very huge.
examples: The astronomical clock.
An astronomical number.
The cost was astronomical.

more.def: Having to do with astronomy; or extremely large.
examples: The telescope is an astronomical tool.
The cost of the rocket was astronomical.
There is an astronomical number of stars.

easy.def: The study of stars and planets.
examples: We learned astronomy.
I like astronomy.
Astronomy is about space.

more.def: The science of the stars, planets and space.
examples: She loves astronomy and often looks at the stars.
In astronomy class we learned why the moon changes shape.
A telescope helps people who enjoy astronomy.

easy.def: Smart and quick to notice.
examples: An astute girl.
The astute detective.
He is astute.

more.def: Clever and quick to understand things.
examples: The astute detective noticed the muddy footprints.
She is an astute observer.
The astute student saw the mistake.
